PART I
Item 1.    Business
Example Manufacturing Corp designs and manufactures industrial sensors. Investors should read the risks described in Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K under the heading Risk Factors.
Item 1A.
Risk Factors
Operational and supply chain risks
We rely on a single third-party supplier for the semiconductor components used in our main product line. Any disruption at this supplier could halt our production for several months.
Our primary manufacturing facility is located in a region exposed to hurricanes, and we have not completed a tested disaster recovery plan for this site.
Example Manufacturing Corp | 2025 Form 10-K | 5

We depend on information technology systems to process orders, and a failure of these systems could interrupt our operations.

We are subject to export control and data protection laws in multiple jurisdictions, and regulators may impose significant fines if we fail to comply with them.
Item 1B.    Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
Item 1C.Cybersecurity
Our Chief Information Security Officer reports quarterly to the Audit Committee on cybersecurity risks and incidents.
In the fourth quarter we experienced a ransomware incident that encrypted systems at two distribution centres and interrupted order processing for nine days.
Item 2.    Properties
We own our headquarters and lease two distribution centres in the United States.
ITEM 3. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS
We are a defendant in a product liability lawsuit relating to a sensor recall, and an adverse outcome could require us to pay damages.
PART II
Item 9A.    Controls and Procedures
Management identified a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting related to user access controls for our enterprise resource planning system.
Management’s remediation plan includes redesigning access reviews, which had not been tested for operating effectiveness as of year end.
Item 9B.    Other Information
None.
